profile.profile: Zhang Xianzi (born April 1986) is a Chinese pop singer of Zhuang ethnicity who is professionally known by her given name Xianzi, meaning 'harp' in English. Born to a musical family, she studied in Maoming and later majored in dance at Guangxi Art College in Nanning. Discovered by a Taiwanese producer in 2005, she achieved widespread popularity across Mainland China and Taiwan following her 2006 duet with Will Pan.
profile.profile_long: Zhang Xianzi was born on April 22, 1986, and is a Chinese singer belonging to the Zhuang ethnicity. Her father worked as a train conductor, and she completed her high school education at No.12 High School in Maoming, Guangdong province. During her high school years, she actively composed several songs with her classmates and published them online, which helped her build an initial following among internet composers in Guangdong province. After finishing high school, she returned to her native Guangxi and attended the Guangxi Art College in Nanning, where she majored in dance. In 2005, her career shifted when she was discovered by Taiwanese producer Zihong Chen, leading to her transition into professional singing. Her breakthrough came in 2006 when she collaborated with Will Pan on the hit song 'I Have to Love', a Chinese-language adaptation of a Korean track by Freestyle. This release propelled her to mainstream fame in both Mainland China and Taiwan. Building on this momentum, she released her first album in 2006, followed by subsequent releases including Wrong Direction, The Queen of Love, Innocent, and Roses In The Wind. In 2007, her contributions were recognized with a nomination for Best Rookie Singer at the Golden Melody Awards in Taiwan, marking a significant milestone in her entertainment career.
